AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/U3 · 澳大利亚作为文: A cultural schema is the cognitive framework a group shares, and it shapes how they read the world; a cultural construct is an idea shaped by society rather than given by nature, such as race, nation or so-called "normality". Discuss how Australia trades off individual freedom (belief, language, cultural practice, spiritual pursuit) against the interests of the community as a whole. The meaning of a sentence is not fixed by the dictionary; it is negotiated between the two parties communicating, and in a cross-cultural context the same wording is often read differently. In analysis, look specifically for places where the speaker meant X but the audience understood Y, and explain how context and stance change meaning. Merely paraphrasing the literal sense of this statement without textual evidence earns nothing.

Three collections of autobiographical essays published by Black Inc., gathering short pieces by Aboriginal, Asian and African Australians about growing up. Use them organised by theme rather than by piece: identity, belonging, racial discrimination, family expectations, language loss. Three autobiographical pieces: Badami writes about how being mocked at school for his name shook his cultural identity; Amy Choi writes about the shift in identity that relearning her mother tongue brought in adulthood; Marlee Silva writes about how volunteering from Cronulla to Papunya overturned her assumptions about Aboriginal identity. The referendum of 27 May 1967 gave the Commonwealth power, by a yes vote of over ninety per cent, to legislate for Aboriginal people and to count them in the census; the 1992 Mabo decision overturned the legal fiction of terra nullius and recognised pre-existing Native Title, with 3 June as Mabo Day. The values booklet the Department of Home Affairs gives visa applicants; most applicants must sign the Australian Values Statement, committing to the rule of law, parliamentary democracy, equality of men and women, freedom of religion and speech, and a "fair go". The Union Jack symbolises the historical tie to Britain, the Southern Cross the position in the southern hemisphere and exploration, and the seven points of the Commonwealth Star the six states plus the territories and future states. AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/U4 · 语言与赋权/文: Different languages carry different cultural classifications: kinship terms, honorifics, expressions of time and direction, colour words, metaphor (using up and down for status, for example). AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/U4 · 语言与赋权/修: The three appeals are ethos (credibility), pathos (emotion) and logos (logic); specific devices include repetition, the rule of three, rhetorical questions, contrast, direct address and metaphor. Eye contact, personal distance, nodding and gesture carry different meanings in different cultures. Covers punctuation (full stops, capitals, commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, colons, semicolons, brackets, exclamation marks), spelling of subject terminology, and common abbreviations and symbols. Metalanguage means the terms used to talk about a text (thesis, tieback); discourse markers signal cause and contrast; collocation means fixed word partnerships. The hard test of a formal register is stripping out colloquial words and contracted forms, and holding the piece together with synonyms, antonyms and lexical chains.

The four moods are declarative (giving information), interrogative (including rhetorical questions), imperative (demanding action) and exclamative (intensifying emotion); a speech deliberately mixes them to move the audience. Nominalisation turns a verb or adjective into a noun, as in decide to decision or diverse to diversity, which makes academic register more compact and objective, though too much of it makes sentences stiff and hard to read.

The four conjunction types are addition (moreover), comparison (whereas), time and cause, and you should not keep reusing the same one. Subject-verb agreement goes wrong most often around parenthetical phrases and collective nouns. Quotation may be direct (copied inside quotation marks) or indirect (person and tense shifted); cohesive reference requires this, it and they to point clearly.

In listening you must catch the main idea, the direction of the argument and specific details at once, using keyword notes rather than full sentences. Appraisal is how language expresses attitude and intensity (engagement, attitude, graduation) and is the tool for analysing evaluative language. Telling fact from opinion and identifying implied meaning and ambiguity are high-frequency short-answer points.

In spoken interaction you must be able to clarify actively ("Do you mean...?") and to recover on the spot; COAT and Task 7 both test this. Register has three levels, familiar, semi-formal and formal, and you must switch by situation; persuasive language includes direct address, rhetorical questions and calls to action. Turn-taking means knowing how to open, to follow on and to hand the talk back, since COAT is an interview and a monologue read from a script will be cut off.

You must recognise the markers of the three registers (contractions, slang, forms of address) and explain why cultural reference, irony and humour can fail across cultures. Differences in politeness norms, eye contact and personal distance are both an object of analysis and a hidden point in the oral marking. AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/学术写作与文本分析/te: The purpose of a discursive essay is to discuss rather than to argue, so claims must stay open: "It could be argued that...", may, might, tends to. AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/学术写作与文本分析/Sp: A speech needs a salutation and acknowledgement, clear signpost sentences, reference back to the audience and a call to action at the end, with one consistent register throughout. AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/学术写作与文本分析/文本: Four things to analyse: persuasive devices (rhetorical questions, repetition, the rule of three, emotional appeal), figurative language (metaphor, imagery, personification), how irony and humour are built, and narrative point of view and person. Evaluate sources for relevance, reliability and validity; paraphrasing must genuinely change sentence structure and vocabulary while keeping the source, since swapping a few words is still plagiarism. AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/学术写作与文本分析/文本: Classified by purpose: analytical texts examine and judge the elements of other texts (reviews, essays, book reviews); imaginative texts entertain or provoke thought through literary elements (novels, poems, plays); interpretive texts explain and interpret people, events and concepts (autobiography, feature articles, documentaries); persuasive texts put a view and influence the reader (advertisements, debates, argumentative essays). AUSMAT May 2026 学习资料/ELD 英语/OLNA 读写与算术测试: One of the three OLNA components; you must reach Level 3 (roughly Year 9 difficulty) to gain the WACE completion certificate, and if you do not pass you must resit that component. The official example test has the same length and structure as the real one. Text types vary widely: novel extracts, websites, tables, timetables, signs, poems, letters, flow charts. The strategy is to read the question first and then locate the specific information in the text; for vocabulary questions guess meaning from context rather than memorising word lists; with an unfamiliar topic, hold on to the keywords in the question instead of relying on background knowledge.

You type your answer on screen, with a maximum of 600 words (the box turns red past that) and no minimum, though too little shows no ability, and you must leave time to edit because spelling and punctuation are marked separately. The test covers reading comprehension (locating specific information, author's purpose, audience, tone, inference), text organisation (indexes, alphabetical, chronological and numerical order, flow charts), vocabulary (synonyms, guessing from context, abbreviations, homonyms) and grammar and punctuation. The seven criteria are audience awareness, structure and organisation, vocabulary, cohesion, sentence structure, punctuation and spelling, and the scores are cumulative: to reach a band you must show the skills of that band and every band below it. Each is marked separately, so a well-structured piece with many punctuation and spelling errors still scores low. Each has a fixed skeleton: a book review follows inform, describe, analyse, evaluate; a formal letter omits addresses, date and heading and needs only a salutation (Dear Sir/Madam) and a sign-off (Yours faithfully); a feature article needs a headline, byline and a hook; a news report uses the inverted pyramid, most important first. Identify the text type before writing, because the wrong skeleton drops you a band.

High-frequency points cluster around confusable structures: could have been rather than could of been, bought versus brought, should have versus should of, converting between active and passive voice, participial clauses, and identifying the four sentence types. It tests synonym substitution, fixed collocations (looking forward to, make contributions to), word-form changes (converting between noun, verb, adjective and adverb) and the position of adverbs in a sentence. For collocation questions, learn words in chunks rather than singly; for word-form questions, first decide which part of speech the gap needs, then compare the candidates in that class.

The official SCSA OLNA practice entry point, offering an example test and a practice test for all three components with the same interface as the real test. You must sign a student agreement before sitting, and breaching the code of conduct is a violation. SCSA runs similarity detection against online content and other students' scripts, and it catches even small amounts, including memorising a model answer from a website or sharing answers with a classmate. Once confirmed it is an immediate fail, and the person who shared the answer is treated the same as the person who copied, so you must write your own from the practice stage.
